hook: Dryland shrub and grass ecosystems behave like matter in phase transitions.
hook_turn: behave like matter in phase transitions.
summary: Deserts, shrublands, and grasslands are separated by abrupt shifts, and the latter two form Turing-like patterns, with fairy circles near the shrub-grass boundary. A cellular automaton built on a trade-off between wide and local resource foraging reproduces these features, and plant traits and patch patterns support the trade-off. The model is simplified, so the match shows consistency with the theory rather than proof of the mechanism.
title: Phase transition in a dryland shrub-grass ecosystem: Emergence through local trade-offs.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
